profile: D_economic:Profile 1 — Economic profile 1: relatively lower household economic position (n=44)
recommended_charts: Cluster-component table; preferred-sector stacked bar; study-field and institution bars
key_officer_insight: Lower relative household economic position; sector, study-field and institution patterns are more diverse and less ICT/private-institution concentrated.
main_caution: Relative position is not poverty status; sparse categories and household-count inconsistencies must remain visible.

profile: D_economic:Profile 2 — Economic profile 2: relatively higher household economic position (n=147)
recommended_charts: Cluster-component table; preferred-sector stacked bar; study-field and institution bars
key_officer_insight: Higher relative household economic position; stronger concentration in ICT study/sector and private institutions.
main_caution: Do not infer affordability or individual course suitability; several categorical tables are sparse.

profile: D_educational_cultural:Profile 1 — Re-entered students, often with degree-educated parents (n=15)
recommended_charts: Educational-characteristic table; job-search, income-source and funding bars
key_officer_insight: Small re-entry group with high active-search prevalence and more varied personal/funding sources.
main_caution: n=15; parental education is a proxy and several related economic tables are sparse.

profile: D_educational_cultural:Profile 2 — State-institution students without work exposure (n=53)
recommended_charts: Educational-characteristic table; job-search and funding stacked bars
key_officer_insight: State-institution students without work exposure, commonly family-supported and often government-funded/free.
main_caution: Cross-dimensional financial variables are related to the separate economic model; do not imply causation.

profile: D_educational_cultural:Profile 3 — Private-institution students without work exposure (n=57)
recommended_charts: Educational-characteristic table; income-source and funding stacked bars
key_officer_insight: Private-institution students without work exposure, with very high family income/funding reliance.
main_caution: Sparse categories; family support is a group prevalence, not true of every member.

profile: D_educational_cultural:Profile 4 — Work-experienced students, mainly in private institutions (n=66)
recommended_charts: Educational-characteristic table; job-search, income-source and income-band bars
key_officer_insight: Work-experienced students, mainly in private institutions, with more mixed personal income sources.
main_caution: Economic characteristics overlap another retained dimension and must be labelled cross-dimensional.

profile: D_motivation:Profile 1 — Consensus motivation profile 1: externally or uncertainly motivated, with moderate study support (n=47)
recommended_charts: Four defining-item stacked bars; employment-contact bar
key_officer_insight: Externally/uncertainly motivated group with a larger descriptive share reporting no useful contacts.
main_caution: Contact difference did not survive FDR; membership uncertainty and single-item constructs must be shown.

profile: D_motivation:Profile 2 — Consensus motivation profile 2: goal-aligned motivation with mixed study confidence and support (n=75)
recommended_charts: Four defining-item stacked bars; employment-contact bar
key_officer_insight: Goal-aligned motivation with mixed confidence/support and comparatively fewer reporting several useful connections.
main_caution: Contact evidence is descriptive, not a headline statistical finding.

profile: D_motivation:Profile 3 — Consensus motivation profile 3: highly self-directed, capable and connected (n=69)
recommended_charts: Four defining-item stacked bars; employment-contact bar
key_officer_insight: Highly self-directed/capable/connected study profile with more respondents reporting several useful contacts.
main_caution: Do not interpret the profile as a guaranteed individual trait; contact evidence is descriptive.

profile: E_learning_orientation:Profile 1 — High perceived education utility and strong learning ambition (n=18)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; small-profile warning
recommended_charts: Three defining-item bars; job-acceptance, network-helpfulness and support bars
key_officer_insight: Higher perceived education usefulness and learning ambition, with descriptive evidence of stricter job conditions and more helpful contacts/support.
main_caution: n=18; no selected profiling comparison survived FDR and several tables are sparse.

profile: E_learning_orientation:Profile 2 — Moderate perceived utility and mixed learning ambition (n=16)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; small-profile warning
recommended_charts: Three defining-item bars; job-acceptance, network-helpfulness and support bars
key_officer_insight: Moderate perceived usefulness/mixed ambition, with descriptively less helpful contacts/support and more job-fair searching among eligible searchers.
main_caution: n=16; conditional search denominator is 11 and no selected comparison survived FDR.

profile: F_employment_security:Profile 1 — Temporary/no-contract employment with uncertain security (n=29)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; median income-band display
recommended_charts: Security-defining stacked bars; income, job-change, satisfaction and training bars
key_officer_insight: Temporary/no-contract and less secure employment, with lower income and less reliance on the job/business as primary personal income.
main_caution: Employment arrangement and satisfaction are related outcomes; conditional work-while-study finding is sparse and non-causal.

profile: F_employment_security:Profile 2 — Predominantly permanent employment with stronger security (n=52)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; median income-band display
recommended_charts: Security-defining stacked bars; income, job-change, satisfaction and training bars
key_officer_insight: Predominantly permanent/stronger-security work, with higher income and greater reliance on regular job/business income.
main_caution: Stronger security does not imply that every member is satisfied or should remain in the job.

recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; small-profile-model warning
recommended_charts: Economic-component table; contacts, connection and self-efficacy median bars
key_officer_insight: Predominantly family/partner-supported non-providers, descriptively less connected to employment contacts and labour-market information.
main_caution: The comparison model includes n=15 in its other profile; no selected profiling finding survived FDR.

recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; small-profile warning
recommended_charts: Economic-component table; contacts, connection and self-efficacy median bars
key_officer_insight: Self-income providers/contributors, descriptively more connected to employment contacts and labour-market information.
main_caution: n=15; results are descriptive and must not be generalized as individual capacities.

profile: G_future_engagement:Profile 1 — Work-and-education engaged, mostly prior work experience (n=35)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; self-efficacy median
key_officer_insight: Work/education-engaged group with stronger self-efficacy, support and labour-market connection and less future uncertainty.
main_caution: Associations are non-causal; the profile does not guarantee readiness for every individual.

profile: G_future_engagement:Profile 2 — Low/uncertain engagement, mostly no prior work experience (n=21)
recommended_dashboard_KPIs: Profile size; model-cohort share; self-efficacy median
key_officer_insight: Low/uncertain engagement group with lower self-efficacy, support and connection and greater future uncertainty.
main_caution: n=21; do not label individuals as deficient or infer unmeasured needs.
